root_cause.text: In ceph_finish_lookup() and ceph_lookup() in fs/ceph/dir.c, the code unconditionally calls d_add(dentry, NULL) on negative dentries without checking d_unhashed(), leading to rehashing of already-hashed dentries and corruption of the dcache hash bucket.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and patch diff explicitly state that both paths (ceph_finish_lookup and ceph_lookup) assume "negative" means "unhashed" but the dentry may already be hashed, and they are fixed by adding a `d_unhashed(dentry)` check before calling `d_add()`. The CVE description confirms that this causes hash list corruption and RCU stalls.

bic_trace_step.reason: In ceph_finish_lookup(), when err == -ENOENT and no trace, the code calls d_add(dentry, NULL) unconditionally in the else branch (if dentry->d_inode is NULL) without checking d_unhashed(). Similarly, in ceph_lookup(), when the dentry is NULL and the directory is complete, it also calls d_add(dentry, NULL) without d_unhashed() check. These match the vulnerability root cause: unconditionally calling d_add on negative dentries without checking if they are already hashed, leading to dcache corruption.
